title: Backpressure-driven audit delivery lag during emergency key rotation — follow-up
creator: Asha Nambiar
description: Summary: During an emergency KMS key rewrap deployed to handle a suspected compromised key, the audit-forwarding pipeline experienced sustained backpressure. The forwarder buffers grew and delivery to the central audit lake was delayed by up to 28 hours for a subset of events. Simultaneously, a partial SSO token invalidation issued during the same window caused a burst of re-authentication flows that increased event fan-out and amplified the forwarder backlog. This ticket captures investigation findings, mitigations applied, and follow-up action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline_summary: 2025-02-18 02:10 UTC: On-call initiated emergency KMS rewrap for key id 'kms-audit-01' after anomalous key usage spike detected.
2025-02-18 02:12 UTC: Audit-forwarder service (audit-forwarder-v3) began returning 429/timeout to upstream producers under load; internal buffers started growing.
2025-02-18 02:15 UTC: Automated SSO token invalidation triggered for sessions signed with the old key; client SDKs initiated mass refresh requests.

2025-02-18 02:20-04:00 UTC: Retry storms and auth refreshes increased per-event amplification ~6x. Backpressure persisted due to single-shard outbound to audit-lake and a long-lived TCP connection limit hit on the collector.
2025-02-18 05:30 UTC: Emergency mitigation - scaled audit-forwarder horizontally and added temporary disk-backed buffer on collectors; delivery resumed but ~40% of events were delayed.
2025-02-19 06:00 UTC: Complete catch-up and verification of delayed events; end-to-end delivery latency window closed (~28 hours for worst-case events).
root_cause: A combination of (1) single_shard egress path from audit-forwarder to central collector that could not absorb a sudden order-of-magnitude increase in traffic, and (2) simultaneous SSO token invalidation that produced a large number of auth refresh events. The emergency KMS rewrap itself was safe, but the coordination window lacked throttling and amplification controls, and the forwarder lacked robust disk-backed spillover and per-customer pacing to prevent head-of-line blocking.
mitigations_applied: Scaled audit-forwarder horizontally by adding 6 instances and temporarily routing to multiple collectors to increase egress capacity.
Enabled disk-backed buffering on collectors to allow controlled spillover and prevent OOM/crash of forwarders.
Rolled back a non-critical SDK auto-retry change that exacerbated amplification during auth failures.
Applied immediate rate-limits on token-refresh endpoints for internal service accounts to flatten the retry curve.
action_items: A1: Implement multi-shard egress for audit-forwarder with automatic shard-splitting when per-shard egress > 70% capacity. Owner: Diego Flores. ETA: 2025-03-15.

A2: Add persistent disk-backed write-ahead queue to forwarder with configurable retention and a safety mode that pauses producers when retention threshold reached. Owner: Melissa Zhang. ETA: 2025-04-01.
A3: Create 'rotation-playbook' that sequences KMS rewrap and session invalidation with coordinated throttles and canary invalidation windows. Owner: Security Oncall (rotating). ETA: 2025-03-01.
A4: Implement adaptive per-identity retry throttling in internal SDKs to limit amplification during mass auth failures. Owner: Client SDK team. ETA: 2025-03-22.
A5: Add a synthetic test harness that simulates simultaneous key rotation + SSO invalidation to validate end-to-end stability on staging. Owner: Reliability Testing. ETA: 2025-03-08.
A6: Update observability: add per-shard egress metrics, buffer retention alerts, and a composite SLO dashboard for audit delivery latency. Owner: Observability team. ETA: 2025-03-10.
A7: Conduct tabletop runbook exercise with Security, Infra, and Client SDK teams to practice coordinated rotations. Owner: Ops. ETA: 2025-03-05.
A8: Post-incident review write-up and customer notification template for delayed-audit events. Owner: Compliance. ETA: 2025-03-04.

acceptance_criteria: Forwarder egress path horizontally scales automatically and maintains per-shard egress < 60% under 6x baseline traffic spike.
Disk-backed forwarder queue prevents in-memory buffer growth beyond safe thresholds and preserves order guarantees for 72 hours of peak traffic.
Rotation-playbook is documented, reviewed by Security & Ops, and validated in a tabletop exercise.
Synthetic harness reproduces the issue on staging and verifies applied mitigations reduce maximum audit-delivery latency to <10 minutes for 99.9% of events during simulated rotations.
